$comment: STORY-024 T12. NFR-API-04: within v1 only additive changes ship. A change that is NOT additive is a deviation, and a deviation that lives only in a commit message is not a gate — it cannot be re-checked, and it never expires. Every entry here is asserted by test/unit/contract-breaking-changes.spec.ts: the recorded change must still be VISIBLE in the current document, so silently reverting one turns the build red and deleting the record has to be a deliberate act. Adding an entry here is not a way to make a gate pass — it is a way to make a deviation legible. A new entry needs a human decision, exactly like a new dependency.

changes.from: the bare resource representation, e.g. Workspace
changes.reason: ResponseEnvelopeInterceptor (T10) wrapped every non-exempt response, but the generated document still described the unwrapped representation. The published contract therefore described a body the server had not sent since T10, and a client generated from it could not read a single response. There was no backward-compatible option: preserving the old shape would have preserved a fiction. The previous-minor proxy was re-authored rather than the change avoided, and both sides of client-previous-minor.spec.ts moved in the same commit — which is precisely why this record exists.

changes.to: WorkspaceListItem[] with a per-item `relationship` of owned|joined, plus the envelope's `pagination` member
changes.reason: NFR-API-03 makes every list cursor-paginated and api-specification.md §1's envelope carries exactly one `pagination` member, which cannot describe two independent cursors over two arrays. STORY-021's requirement is that a caller can tell an owned workspace from a joined one; that is preserved per item rather than by shape, so the switcher still groups and badges them with one filter. The one-owned invariant caps `owned` at a single row, so `joined` was always the only unbounded half. There was no additive option: leaving the two arrays would have left the route permanently outside NFR-API-03. The previous-minor proxy was deliberately NOT rewritten this time, so the N-1 comparison shows the break instead of hiding it.

NFR-API-05 states that all durations are integer milliseconds with a `_ms` suffix. No reference document ever named this field; it was invented in code during STORY-016 and published, so the taxonomy sweep in money-and-formats.spec carried a named exemption for it (decision D14) with a guard asserting the exemption still described a real field. That guard has now fired. Both the unit and the name change together, because a renamed unit keeping the old name is worse than either alone: a consumer reading `expires_in_seconds` and getting 600000 would show a ten-thousand-minute expiry.

changes.to: data_source: live|demo|mixed or null, where null means nothing was measured
changes.reason: Owner decision 2 of 2026-10-08 (plans-7day/decisions-2026-10-08.md) approved this as a breaking change. The workspace summary used a two-value live|demo marker while the per-project surfaces (matrix, scorecards, growth map) use the single vocabulary live|demo|mixed|null, and the two could not both stay: a figure backed by both real and demo captures was forced into one label, and an engine with nothing measured was reported as demo. One vocabulary everywhere was the owner's call. A typed consumer that switched exhaustively on live|demo now has two more cases, so this is not additive. The previous-minor proxy does not cover this route, so there is no baseline to rewrite.

changes.from: a wallet response with no auto-top-up member
changes.to: a wallet response whose REQUIRED data.auto_topup carries { enabled, pack_key, threshold, max_per_cycle, used_this_cycle, disabled_reason }
changes.reason: Owner decision of 2026-10-08 (relayed in the checkpoint-3 fix-pass task text) approved making auto_topup a REQUIRED member of the wallet response as a breaking change. api-specification.md section 3 says the wallet carries the auto-top-up config, and a response that sometimes omits it would force every client to guess between off and unknown, so the field is required rather than optional. A consumer generated from the previous contract and a strict response validator would reject the new body, so this is not additive. The previous-minor proxy does not cover this route, so there is no baseline to rewrite.

changes.to: { data: CreditPack[], pagination, meta } with the standard cursor and limit query; ordered by (sort_order, credits, key)
changes.reason: Owner-approved under the NEW-D-1 cursor-envelope rule: NEW-D-1 AC3 in the signed-off plan (plans-7day/track-plans.json) says every list response uses the cursor envelope, matching api-specification.md section 3 and not the demo's bare arrays; the checkpoint-4 fix-pass task text restated it for this route. It is not a numbered item in plans-7day/decisions-2026-10-08.md. Making pagination a REQUIRED response member and accepting cursor/limit (the request schema is strict) means a strict response validator built from the old contract rejects the new body, so this is not additive. The earlier comment arguing for a bare array because the catalog is a handful of rows reversed the criterion and is withdrawn. The previous-minor proxy does not cover this route, so there is no baseline to rewrite.

changes.from: the add-ons the workspace holds: { id, kind, quantity (positive), unit_price_usd, grant, active_from, active_until }
changes.to: the purchasable catalog, one item per add-on kind: { kind, display_name, unit_price_usd, purchasable, quantity (0 when none held), grant, id|null, active_from|null, active_until|null }
changes.reason: Owner decision of 2026-10-08 (decisions-2026-10-08.md, STORY-076b line): GET /billing/addons also lists the purchasable catalog with prices. A workspace holding nothing must read the unit prices before it buys, and check:no-cost-literals forbids the control from carrying them. The item gains required members (display_name, purchasable) and id, active_from and quantity become nullable or zero for a kind not held, so a typed consumer of the held-only list breaks; this is not additive. Recorded at checkpoint-4 because it was missing from this file. The previous-minor proxy does not cover this route.

changes.scope: addAddon (POST /v1/billing/addons): the meaning of the request's quantity
changes.from: quantity is the desired TOTAL of the add-on after the change, not an increment
changes.to: quantity is the number of units to ADD to the held quantity; the held quantity plus quantity may not exceed 100; the response's quantity_requested is still the total the Stripe item was set to
changes.reason: Owner decision of 2026-10-08 (decisions-2026-10-08.md, STORY-076b line): POST quantity ADDS to the held quantity. The request SHAPE is unchanged ({ kind, quantity }), so a client written for the total semantics still validates and silently buys the wrong number of units (holding 2 and sending 3 now yields 5, not 3); that silent change of meaning is why it is breaking and why it is recorded. The assertion below pins the operation's response shape; the changed meaning itself lives in the request schema's description and cannot be asserted from the document's property names. Retry safety is carried by the Idempotency-Key, not by the number. The previous-minor proxy does not cover this route.

changes.from: { data: ApiKey[], meta } with no pagination member and no cursor/limit query; every key in one response, ordered by created_at DESC, id
changes.to: { data: ApiKey[], pagination, meta } with the standard cursor and limit query; ordered by (created_at DESC, id DESC) with a microsecond-precision cursor key
changes.reason: Lead's call of 2026-10-09 (decisions-2026-10-08.md, section after checkpoint 5): GET /v1/api-keys moves to the cursor envelope under NEW-D-1 AC3, which in the signed-off plan (plans-7day/track-plans.json) says every list response uses the cursor envelope, matching api-specification.md section 3; the same decision says to record it as a breaking change. Making pagination a REQUIRED response member and accepting cursor/limit (the request schema is strict) means a strict response validator built from the old contract rejects the new body, and a client that relied on one response carrying every key now sees at most the page limit, so this is not additive. The previous-minor proxy does not cover this route, so there is no baseline to rewrite.

changes.task: NEW-D-3 / NEW-D-1 (checkpoint-4 audit-log id, recorded at checkpoint-5)
changes.from: an id derived from the row's hash material, which would leak the audit chain (row N's prev_hash is row N-1's row_hash)
changes.to: the row's audit_log.seq as a decimal string matching ^[0-9]{1,18}$, the same value the opaque cursor is keyed on
changes.reason: Lead's call of 2026-10-09, approved by the owner (decisions-2026-10-08.md, section after checkpoint 5): the audit-log id becomes the row seq. Exposing either hash would leak the chain, and audit_log has no per-row uuid column; adding one is a schema change deferred to week 2. The id's value and format change (a hash-like string becomes a short decimal string), so a client that stored or pattern-matched old ids breaks, and seq is a global sequence so ids are monotonic across workspaces, a trade-off accepted for week 1. The request and envelope shapes are unchanged; the assertion pins the item's property names and the id pattern lives in the schema. The previous-minor proxy does not cover this route, so there is no baseline to rewrite.
